To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the history of race and racism in sport science is a significant influence on the current use of race in sport science, and the history of race in sport is a significant influence in the history of race within sport science.

(1) the history of race in sport science is complex; (2) the history of sport science is a key factor in understanding how race is constructed and understood in the field; (3) sport science has a history of racism; and (4) sport scientists continue to use the concept of race to explain athletic performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social and historical construction of the body and the ways in which the body is represented, understood and used in society.
the relationship between scientific knowledge and social power.
the social construction of the category ‘race’, and its impact on the production of scientific knowledge in sport science.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence for racial differences in athletic performance is weak, and that the differences that do exist are likely to be due to environmental factors.

there is no scientific evidence to support the notion of ‘racial’ differences in sport, but the history and social construction of race in the field of sport science, combined with the pressures of the professional environment, has created the conditions for the normalisation of scientific racism.
the scientific evidence is insufficient to support a genetic basis for racial differences in athletic performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sport science is an example of a field of knowledge production that has a long history of scientific racism.

the ‘race’ concept has been used in sport to create a discourse of black athletic physical superiority that is not based on scientific evidence, but on folk genetics and the history of sport and science.
we need to be very careful in how we use the word ‘race’.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scientific community needs to do a better job of educating people on the science of race and the dangers of using it to explain human behavior and performance in sport.
the scientific community needs to be more aware of the potential consequences of their work.
we can use the same methods and tools that we use to measure athletic performance to also measure racial bias.
